/-!
# Conjecture 2.80

by S. N. Chernikov

Does every non-trivial group satisfying the normalizer condition contain a
non-trivial abelian normal subgroup?

A group $G$ satisfies the normalizer condition if every proper subgroup $H < G$
is properly contained in its normalizer, $H < N_G(H)$. In Mathlib this is
`NormalizerCondition G`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.docstring:
Does every non-trivial group $G$ satisfying the normalizer condition (every proper
subgroup $H < G$ satisfies $H < N_G(H)$) contain a non-trivial abelian normal
subgroup $N \ne 1$?

The hypothesis `Nontrivial G` excludes the trivial group, which satisfies the
normalizer condition vacuously but has no non-trivial subgroup.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (Prop: ∀ G nontrivial group with the normalizer condition, i.e. every proper subgroup H satisfies H < N_G(H), ∃ normal subgroup N ≠ ⊥ that is abelian/commutative); the normalizer condition must be defined explicitly (not in Mathlib), and 'non-trivial' should be Nontrivial G on the group and N ≠ ⊥ on the subgroup, with answer(sorry) since the problem is open.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ nontrivial group G with the normalizer condition, ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N ≠ ⊥ ∧ IsMulCommutative N. This matches the source: answer(True) is the positive answer, quantifiers are all right of answer(sorry), 'non-trivial' is Nontrivial G on the group and N ≠ ⊥ on the subgroup, 'abelian' is IsMulCommutative ↥N (repo idiom from Kourovka/20_76.lean). c07 was chosen as base because it uses Mathlib's NormalizerCondition (verified by Iff.rfl to be ∀ H : Subgroup G, H < ⊤ → H < H.normalizer, i.e. exactly the classical normalizer condition), uses [Nontrivial G] and G : Type in line with the other Kourovka files, and its docstring spells out the normalizer condition and explains why Nontrivial G is needed (the trivial group satisfies the condition vacuously and has no non-trivial subgroup — checked in a scratch file). Only cosmetic edits were made.

This is incorrect: Mathlib has `NormalizerCondition G := ∀ H : Subgroup G, H < ⊤ → H < normalizer H` (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Basic.lean), which is precisely the standard definition. Since the repository rules (AGENTS.md/STATEMENTS.md) require searching Mathlib and reusing existing definitions rather than duplicating them, I used the Mathlib definition instead of adding a bespoke one. The mathematical content of the slot is otherwise exactly as the table describes.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.80

by S. N. Chernikov

Does every non-trivial group satisfying the normalizer condition contain a
non-trivial abelian normal subgroup?

A group $G$ satisfies the normalizer condition if every proper subgroup $H < G$
is properly contained in its normalizer, $H < N_G(H)$. In Mathlib this is
`NormalizerCondition G`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.80»

/--
Does every non-trivial group $G$ satisfying the normalizer condition (every proper
subgroup $H < G$ satisfies $H < N_G(H)$) contain a non-trivial abelian normal
subgroup $N \ne 1$?

The hypothesis `Nontrivial G` excludes the trivial group, which satisfies the
normalizer condition vacuously but has no non-trivial subgroup.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.80» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Nontrivial G], NormalizerCondition G →
      ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N ≠ ⊥ ∧ IsMulCommutative N := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.80»

items: Used Mathlib's `NormalizerCondition G` (every proper subgroup H < ⊤ satisfies H < N_G(H)) rather than a bespoke definition; verified by `Iff.rfl` in a scratch check that it unfolds to the expected statement.
'Abelian' is expressed as `IsMulCommutative N` on the subgroup coerced to a type, following the existing idiom in FormalConjectures/Kourovka/20_76.lean.

'Non-trivial group' is `[Nontrivial G]`; this is necessary because the trivial group satisfies the normalizer condition vacuously and has no non-trivial subgroup (checked in scratch). 'Non-trivial subgroup' is `N ≠ ⊥`.
Quantified over `G : Type` (universe 0), following the convention of the other Kourovka files (1_40, 1_74, 19_25, 20_76).
Positive answer `answer(True)` corresponds to 'yes'; `answer(False)` corresponds to the existence of a non-trivial group with the normalizer condition and no non-trivial abelian normal subgroup.

reviewer_notes: The decomposition note claims the normalizer condition 'is not in Mathlib' and must be defined explicitly; this is incorrect for this checkout — `NormalizerCondition G` exists in Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Basic.lean with precisely the definition the note gives. Per AGENTS.md/STATEMENTS.md (search Mathlib before adding a definition), the final file uses the Mathlib predicate rather than a bespoke duplicate; the docstring states the condition explicitly in words. Candidates c02–c04 inlined the same formula, which is definitionally equal and equally faithful. Minor variations among candidates (c06 uses `Type*`, c01 uses `Nontrivial G →`, c05 orders conjuncts differently) are all faithful; `Type` was kept to follow the existing Kourovka files' convention. No candidate omitted the slot and no omission reasons needed weighing.
